title: Koszul regularity under an equal-length change of ideal generators
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_r\in A$ with $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], then $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ is Koszul-regular. Equivalently their Koszul complexes have the same positive-degree vanishing condition. No proper-ideal, local, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed; the empty tuple and zero ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), part (3); used twice in the proof of Tag 07CZ (lemma-koszul-independence-presentation).

proof.text: Put $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ and $B=A/I$. By [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis], the classes of the $a_i$ form a $B$-basis of $I/I^2$, since the $a_i$ are Koszul-regular and generate $I$. Write $\theta:B^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\sim}I/I^2$ for this basis isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), proof, first two paragraphs and final sentence of part (3); conormal basis from Tag 062I (lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular), first paragraph.

proof.text: Because every $b_j$ belongs to $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, choose $c_{ij}\in A$ with $b_j=\sum_i c_{ij}a_i$. Set $C=(c_{ij})$ and $t(e_j)=\sum_i c_{ij}e_i$. The functionals $\alpha(e_i)=a_i$ and $\beta(e_i)=b_i$ satisfy $\alpha\circ t=\beta$ by evaluation on each $e_j$. If $\overline C$ denotes reduction modulo $I$, then $\theta\overline C$ sends $e_j$ to the class of $b_j$ in $I/I^2$. These classes generate: every $x\in I$ is a linear combination of the $b_j$, and reducing its coefficients modulo $I$ gives the required expression modulo $I^2$. Thus $\overline C:B^{\oplus r}\to B^{\oplus r}$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), proof, first two paragraphs and final sentence of part (3); conormal basis from Tag 062I (lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular), first paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective] over the commutative ring $B$ to the finite free module $B^{\oplus r}$ and its surjective endomorphism $\overline C$. It is invertible. If $N$ is the matrix of its inverse, then $N\overline C=1$, hence $\det(N)\det(\overline C)=1$. Therefore $\delta=\det(C)$ has unit image in $B$ (determinants commute with reduction). This also covers the zero quotient ring and the $0\times0$ determinant, which is $1$.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), proof, first two paragraphs and final sentence of part (3); conormal basis from Tag 062I (lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular), first paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-substitution-unit-mod-ideal] to $a,b,t$: the ideals agree, $\alpha t=\beta$, and $\det(t)$ is a unit modulo $I$, as just proved. The exterior-power comparison $K_\bullet(b)\to K_\bullet(a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By the definition of quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], it preserves vanishing of homology in every degree. The positive-degree homology of $K_\bullet(a)$ vanishes by the hypothesis and [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]; hence that of $K_\bullet(b)$ vanishes, giving the required regularity. Applying the same implication with the tuples exchanged gives the stated equivalence.

The item statement is unchanged and matches 066A(3) with no added hypothesis. The only citer, lem-sfb-koszul-polynomial-presentation-independence step 6, uses it in exactly this form. Step 1 cites lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis (the 0CEM+062I conormal basis); its hypotheses match exactly, and it is accepted as an off-unit generic tool. Step 2 is elementary and checks out: with t(e_j)=sum_i c_ij e_i we get alpha t = beta, theta C-bar sends e_j to the class of b_j, and C-bar is surjective. Step 3 cites the Mathlib leaf 05G8 over B=A/I; the determinant of C-bar is a unit, and B=0 and r=0 are covered. Step 4 uses the new node, the quasi-isomorphism definition in def-weil-abstract-derived-category and 062E(3); the hypotheses are symmetric, so the equivalence holds. Its direction K(b)->K(a) is correct for the DAG's derivation convention; Stacks writes the map the other way. I checked that it is true without regularity: I kills both homologies by the null-homotopies, delta acts invertibly on homology mod I, wedge t is an isomorphism after inverting delta, and localization is exact.
